newsitem.title: USA: Cinergy, Ill. cooperative sign power deal.
newsitem.headline: Cinergy, Ill. cooperative sign power deal.

text.p: Cinergy Corp, in a drive to add customers outside its Cincinnati service territory, said Wednesday it has signed a deal to provide all the electricity needed by Southwestern Electricity Cooperative, Inc (SWEC).
The agreement is to run for five years, with service expected to start in April, Cinergy said in a statement.
Southwestern, with a peak load of 68 megawatts, is a non-profit utility serving much of southwestern Illinois and the eastern part of the St Louis metropolitan area.
Southwestern currently receives power from Soyland Power Inc, a cooperative based in Decatur, Ill., serving 21 member systems, of which Southwestern is one.

"The cooperative's buyout from Soyland Power and its interest in the Clinton nuclear power plant will require capital financing of roughly $40 million," the statement said, adding that the buyout will be paid off within five years.
The 930-megawatt Clinton power plant, in Clinton, Ill., is operated by Illinois Power Co, a unit of Illinova Corp.
Cinergy, based in Cincinnati, Ohio, is an investor-owned utility serving some 1.4 million electric and 450,000 gas customers in Indiana, southwestern Ohio and northern Kentucky.
Cinergy said the power service agreement with Southwestern could eventually be expanded to include natural gas and propane sales and some maintenance services for customer-owned equipment.
